fullDaySay: You push through the doors into open air. Haven grounds — tents, a fire pit, worn paths. The world is that way.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 1 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 2 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.

💧 A woman, maybe 30s, with a gap-toothed grin returns with water: +3 clean.
💧 A woman, maybe 30s, with a wiry build returns with water: +4 clean.

"Hey." A woman, maybe 30s, with a gap-toothed grin settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A woman, maybe 30s, with a gap-toothed grin.)
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1200 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
A person, maybe 30s, with ink-stained fingers and A man, maybe 50s, with a limp are comparing scars like trading cards.
🔍 A crouches over colonies of umbrella-like leaves, single lemon-sized fruit hidden underneath, studying it a moment before moving on. (1/3 looks)
★ IDENTIFIED: Inajá. Yellow fruit bunches on a fat-based palm. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
A woman, maybe 40s brought you a sample. The Journal grows.
Emmett and Brian lingered over the fire together.

— DAY 2 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
The fire burns low. One new line in the journal: Inajá — named and noted.
👀 You caught the man in his 50s, with a limp rehearsing — muttering details about Denver under their breath before the evening fire, like someone cramming for a part.
📓 Journal: jotted down what they said (A man, maybe 50s, with a limp).
Hosny Khairy reads the sky: clear tomorrow, cold.
A man, maybe 60s, with thick glasses will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.
You step into the Haven hall.
📋 A man, maybe 60s, with thick glasses — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
A person, maybe 30s, with deep-set eyes shakes their head. "Ask someone who trusts you." (Trust too low.)
📋 A person, maybe 20s — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
A woman, maybe 30s, with a gap-toothed grin mutters something under their breath. You catch only the last word: "again."
(Talking costs a little energy — 10 kcal a conversation. Small talk is cheap; going deep costs time, not more food.)
Hunger gnaws. The pack is thin — work the green, haul it back, get it named at camp. That's the whole game.
"Emmett," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Emmett." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Emmett).
"Jae," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Jae." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Jae).
"Nikos," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Nikos." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Nikos).

Travel 1 tile to grove.
— Nut trees —
Bark stripped at deer height on a young hickory — teeth, winter, hunger. Somebody winters here. Maybe you will too.
Something big is moving in the woods. The birds went quiet.
You see smoke on the horizon. Stonebridge — 10 people, 3 days in. foragers, by the look of it. They know 5 plants — 5 new to you. They've been here the whole time.
You catch fragments by the fire — A woman, maybe 40s telling A woman, maybe 30s, with a gap-toothed grin about Jae. It's barely the same story now. That's what fires do.
You catch fragments by the fire — A person, maybe 30s, with ink-stained fingers telling A man, maybe 50s, with a limp about you. The story's getting bigger than what happened.
You catch fragments by the fire — Nikos telling A person, maybe 30s, with ink-stained fingers about A man, maybe 60s, with thick glasses. The details have shifted. Nobody seems to mind.
Unfamiliar unknown nuts — into the bag. (Unknowns lump together; sort them at camp.)
Journal: Riparian ground. Water means life, and lunch.
📓 Journal: you UNDERSTAND **Green Thumb, Literally**. It resonates with: something unnamed, something unnamed.
A shot in the dark — you take what's green: 4× unknown nuts. Into the bag, unnamed. (Not food until identified — sort them at camp.) This patch is picked clean — it'll recover in a few days.
Travel 1 tile to Haven.
1 unprocessed haul onto the counter — the clock is ticking.
Someone by the fire nods at the counter. "We pool food here. Keep what you need for the road — the rest feeds everyone, once it's food."
Nobody at the fire knows your haul any better than you do. It'll be your own hands that teach you.
You walk back into Haven. 4 Codex entries. The village is glad to see you.
A man, maybe 60s, with thick glasses picks through the bag, frowning. Nothing they can name with confidence. (8 ticks)

Jae spends the afternoon with the tree with lobed leaves and oval nuts in scaly caps — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. Raw, it knots the stomach. Cooked... fine. The fire learns the rule before the name: cook it, or else.
From the lumped bag: White Oak Acorns — named, and out.
★ IDENTIFIED: White Oak Acorns. White oak acorn. Lobed leaves, sweet acorns. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
💡 You see it again in your mind: a tree with lobed leaves and oval nuts in scaly caps. Jae's words land on the memory like a label. White Oak Acorns. Of course.
A person, maybe 30s, with ink-stained fingers was watching. Now they know White Oak Acorns too.
The Journal notes it: White Oak Acorns — cook it, or else. (Jae tested it.)
A woman, maybe 30s, with a wiry build: "Walked past a good stand of a fountain of sharp-edged grass smelling of lemon. Worth remembering where."
Jae traded something with someone for something else. The barter economy stirs.
Sanne and Jae lingered over the fire together.
Nina and Jae lingered over the fire together.
🍽️ Hosny sets the sharing basket down by the fire instead of the pantry. "Full shelves don't need my little more."

Fresh-cut stems on the northeast ground — someone else is working turf your crews use. (Stonebridge's foragers, most likely. You walk the ground yourself: it's thinner than your crews alone could strip it.)

Fresh food keeps days, not weeks. Smoke it over a fire to make it last.
